title: Cello
summary: Cello notes played through a computed cello body. Limits first: A3 and the low notes are too dark, several notes are too clean, and the stopped notes sit off pitch. Every note drives a computed spruce and maple shell body with an air cavity, a finite-width hair bow, the measured rosin friction law of Woodhouse and Galluzzo (2025, eq. 13) and the printed 116 mm after-length. E2 sits 5.8 c flat of equal temperament and E3 7.0 c flat (the median in 0.1 s windows over 0.6-1.95 s on its posted clip, with the other three strings on its bridge; the grader's pitch reads it 8.2 c flat), each after one finger move and one residual-flexibility row and with its bow moved to 1/11 of its sounding length; F5's bow is at 1/11 too, which removes its line at a third of its pitch. Eb4 is rendered at 47944 Hz, a rate chosen on its 11-04 page to remove time-step lines, plays with the body's wood loss raised 3.25 times, near the printed damping, and has its bow at 1/11 of its sounding length too; with the endpin, the printed bar and 24-layer ribs it scores 9 of 14 where it scored 11 with 6-layer ribs, and 9 again with its bow force recomputed on that body (0.251 N where it was 0.291 N): its harmonics and short-time spectrum are outside their rulers, its fifth and sixth harmonics sit 2.3 and 4.1 dB over the recording's and its eighth 33.2 dB under it (re the first, 0.5-1.6 s), and above 5 kHz it reads -62.7 dB re total against -32.1 dB in the recording; its line at 301 Hz reads 52 dB under its first harmonic while one as far over its note, at 326 Hz, reads 47 dB under it, its note is 0.7 dB too clean (3.8 dB with 6-layer ribs), and its start is fast now: its attack reads 118 ms against 411 (437 before its force was recomputed). D3 carries its string's measured torsion (758 Hz, 1.8 kg/s, Q 34), which moves it 1.0 c flat and off the render clock; on the body with the endpin and the printed bar on 6-layer ribs its attack reads 387 ms against 381, from a shelf 3 to 6 dB under the held level to 0.35 s rather than the recording's slow rise, and its first two harmonics stay swapped; with the cello's other three strings (C2, G2, A3) unbowed on its bridge, on 6-layer ribs, it scores 14 of 14 as before, its second harmonic goes from 4.6 dB over the first to 10.3 dB under it (the recording's is 7.5 dB under) and its centroid from 358 to 311 Hz (the recording's is 215), but the shelf is gone and its attack reads 91 ms, its note reads 11.6 dB too dirty where it was 4.1, and a line at 198.3 Hz rings at -33 dB re its first harmonic, 11 dB over the recording's strongest low line. With its ribs meshed in 24 layers it scores 13 of 14 where it scored 14: its partial frequencies cross their ruler outward (in windows of eight periods its period ranges over 4.1 c, against 0.9 c with 6-layer ribs and 2.0 c in the recording), its seventh and eleventh harmonics rise 16.2 and 9.3 dB, to 10.6 and 17.1 dB over the recording's, and its fourth falls 15.7 dB, to 14.6 dB under it (re the first, 1.0-2.4 s), its line at 198 Hz falls 7.5 dB, to -40.9 dB re its first harmonic (0.5-2.4 s), its centroid is 403 Hz against 215, and its note reads 11.6 dB too dirty. C2 now plays the s8 shell the other pages play, with the endpin, the printed bar, its ribs meshed in 24 layers and the cello's other three strings (D3, G2, A3) unbowed on its bridge: it scores 5 of 14 where it scored 7 with its bowed string alone (8 on its old shell, 6 on the s8 shell with 6-layer ribs); its partial frequencies and its odd/even balance leave their rulers (the balance reads +14.8 dB against +0.3 in the recording) because its third harmonic rises 8.0 dB, 1.1 Hz from the G2 string's second partial (a coincidence, not traced); its attack reads 270 ms against 78 on the page before and 18 in the recording, it reads 9.7 dB too clean (harmonics-to-noise 39.8 dB against 30.1), and its 11th and 12th harmonics sit 42 and 45 dB under the recording's, re its third. G2 carries the endpin, the printed bar and the cello's other three strings (D3, C2, A3) unbowed on its bridge, and with its ribs meshed in 24 layers it scores 12 of 14 where it scored 13 with 6-layer ribs: its second harmonic sits 1.8 dB under its first (the recording's 5.7 dB under, 0.75-1.6 s), its odd/even balance comes close to the recording's (0.4 dB against 3.0) and its pitch holds steadily (the period ranges over 1.4 c, the recording's 3.3 c), but its short-time spectrum crosses its ruler outward, the D3 string rings at 146 Hz at -30 dB, the note reads 8.9 dB too dirty (harmonics-to-noise 27.4 dB against 36.3), its eighth harmonic sits 35.6 dB under the recording's, and above 5 kHz it reads -68.3 dB re total against -47.3 dB in the recording. E2 carries the endpin, the printed bar, 24-layer ribs and, with its C string still stopped by the finger, the cello's other three strings (D3, G2, A3) unbowed on its bridge: it scores 6 of 14 where it scored 5 with its stopped string alone (8 with 6-layer ribs). Its odd/even balance (-5.8 dB against +1.5 in the recording) and its harmonics-to-noise (31.4 dB against 30.1, where it read 43.2) enter their rulers for a reason the strings' own lines do not explain, and its partial trajectories leave theirs. The D3 string rings at 146.1 Hz, -31 dB re the strongest bin; the second harmonic no longer leads the first (1.4 dB under it, the recording's 5.5 dB over); the harmonics rearrange (the mean distance from the recording's levels 21.7 to 27.5 dB); the level drifts 1.5 dB either way and the burst near the body's 190 Hz mode returns to -42 dB. E3 now carries the endpin, the printed bar and 24-layer ribs as well and scores 5 of 14 where it scored 6, and 5 again with its bow force recomputed on that body (1.924 N where it was 1.467 N): its odd/even balance is outside its ruler and its start is fast (-3 dB re the held level at 0.1 s, against 0.375 s in the recording); at the old force the 24-layer body made its pitch drop three times in the clip, to as much as 23.5 c flat of equal temperament (with the endpin and the bar on 6-layer ribs, a render not posted, it did not), and with the recomputed force it held 4.9 to 8.1 c flat on its posted clip (the same read, median 6.2 c). With the cello's other three strings (D3, G2, A3) unbowed on its bridge, its C string still stopped by the finger, E3 scores 6 of 14 where it scored 5: spectral flux crosses its ruler inward (1.082 to 1.016, ruler 1.022), by 0.006, while its odd/even balance reads 12.6 dB against 0.4 in the recording (10.8 before) and it sits 7.0 c flat (4.8 to 8.7 c flat by the same read); the D3 string rings as a stable line at 146.1 Hz, -44.0 dB re the strongest bin (the recording's line is -43.2 dB at 146.2 Hz, the page without the strings' -56.2 dB at 145.1 Hz). F5 now carries the endpin, the printed bar and 24-layer ribs as well and scores 6 of 15 where it scored 9, and 6 again with its bow force recomputed on that body (0.417 N where it was 0.331 N): its second harmonic leads the first by 5.1 dB while the third to the twelfth sit 10 to 81 dB under it (0.7-1.7 s), which puts its centroid inside its ruler (1245 Hz against 1187) but leaves it 16.8 dB too clean, and its odd/even balance, spectral distance, band envelope and wavelet spectrum are outside their rulers. With the cello's other three strings (D3, C2, G2) unbowed on its bridge, its A string still stopped by the finger, and a 96 kHz render clock decimated to 48 kHz, F5 scores 6 of 15 again and no row crosses its ruler: its odd/even balance reads -14.2 dB against 0.0 in the recording (-15.4 before), its centroid 1233 Hz against 1187, spectral flux reads further (1.398 to 1.630, ruler 1.021), and the D3 string rings as a stable line at 146.5 Hz, -50.2 dB re the first harmonic (the recording's line is -45.0 dB at 152.2 Hz). A3 carries the endpin, the printed bar, 24-layer ribs, the cello's other three strings (D3, C2, G2) unbowed on its bridge and a 96 kHz render clock decimated to 48 kHz, and scores 9 of 14 where it scored 8: its cepstral envelope crosses its ruler inward; the ribs alone gave 10, the 96 kHz clock alone costs a row (brightness crosses back out), and the strings leave the count at 9 while they take its fourth harmonic down 11.6 dB, to 15.1 dB under the recording's (re the first, 0.5-1.2 s), its odd/even balance reads -12.3 dB against -5.5 dB in the recording and its centroid 323 Hz against 868; the note reads 4.0 dB too clean, and above 5 kHz it reads -59.7 dB re total against -26.8 dB in the recording. D3 and A3 keep 512 body modes, the others 256.
physics_present: a computed cello shell body from published plate geometry and wood data: spruce top, maple back and ribs, a 12.5 mm-class table, a 19 g bridge and 256 computed modes (D3 and A3 keep 512; D3's last mode was about 4.3 kHz on 6-layer ribs); on all eight pages the ribs are meshed in 24 layers (5.1 mm), the most the shell's per-component cap admits, because 12 layers were not converged (from 12 to 24 layers the first 100 coupled modes moved a median 0.60 % and modes 101 to 257 1.61 %, against limits of 0.3 and 1 % registered before the runs); whether 24 layers is converged is not measured; the pages had 6 layers (20.3 mm) before
an enclosed air cavity through a physical neck, and f-holes placed from printed caliper measurements of the Castelbarco Stradivari (Library of Congress)
the measured Kaplan string rows (Mansour 2016): tension, mass, bending stiffness and loss factors for the string played, with the bridge and bow flexibility

the exact static residual flexibility of each string's omitted bending modes (`residual-flexibility exact-static-green`): the row adds the string's omitted modes as one static compliance at the bridge and at a finger, with no fitted number; A3, C2, D3 and G2 carry it with its bow counterpart, E2 and E3 carry the support row alone (on 6-layer ribs it took the E3 note 4.5 c flat and its 180 Hz line down 11.6 dB, on the page rendered 11-05, and the E2 note 4.8 c sharp), and Eb4 and F5 carry neither

the string's measured torsion on D3 (`torsion-measured mansour-2016-kaplan-cello-d3-open`; Mansour, Woodhouse and Scavone 2016, Part 2, section 2.2): 10 twist modes at multiples of 758 Hz, a characteristic impedance of 1.8 kg/s and Q 34 on every mode, a non-dispersive line from the nut to the bridge station with the after-length untwisted and no gas drag added. The binding of that string to this one is a reading of the two papers (Part 2 names neither the string's make nor its length; the row binds it to Part 1's Kaplan Solutions D3 at 0.69 m). On the body with the endpin and the printed bar on 6-layer ribs, before the other strings were added, it moves D3 1.0 c flat (146.91 Hz) and off the render clock (326.73 samples a period, steady to 1.4 c), moves H2 to H10 by 2.9 dB or less re the first and leaves 14 of 14 rows inside
a bow of finite width (a 10 mm ribbon) with hair compliance, driven by a gesture schedule of ramp, hold and lift; on D3 and A3 the bow force follows the bow speed through the start of the stroke

on E3, E2, F5 and Eb4 the bow sits 1/11 of the sounding length from the bridge, as on the open pages (25.1 mm of 276.6 mm, 50.1 mm of 551.0 mm, 20.0 mm of 220.5 mm and 44.4 mm of 487.9 mm), with the force from Schelleng's limits at that distance (the maximum goes as v/beta and the minimum as v/beta^2: Mansour, Woodhouse and Scavone 2017, eqs 3-5). The force is the geometric mean of the window, a rule chosen for these pages and stated before any render (E3 1.92 N in 0.805 to 4.60 N, F5 0.42 N in 0.098 to 1.78 N on the A string and Eb4 0.25 N in 0.035 to 1.78 N on the A string, each window on the engine's own bridge admittance of that page's shell in vacuo, `--body-response-only`, without the strings, the cavity's pressure feedback or the radiation reaction, on the 24-layer body with the endpin and the printed bar, Eb4's with its raised wood loss; the same arithmetic on that body's table of coupled modes with the sound holes open, the air mode included, gives 1.69, 0.355 and 0.265 N; E2 keeps 1.50 N in 0.49 to 4.60 N from the earlier body's shell table, because no wood pack in the tree has a band that reaches 82.4 Hz, so the engine's harmonic route refuses the window at E2's f0 and its force is not recomputed). The open pages' forces sit higher in their windows by the same arithmetic (A3's 0.7071 N and D3's 1.0 N at 0.80 and 0.78 on a log scale from the minimum to the maximum), F5's old 0.7071 N was 1.10 times Schelleng's maximum at its old distance, and Eb4's old 0.7071 N was inside its window then, at 0.85 on that scale
the measured rosin friction curve (Woodhouse and Galluzzo 2025, eq. 13) on every note
the printed 116 mm after-length, bridge to tailpiece (Fouilhe and Houssay, SMAC 2013), on every note

stopped notes: a rigid finger stop on the fingerboard (Issanchou 2017) at 1e12 N/m on the C string (E2, E3) and 1e13 N/m on the A string (F5, and Eb4 as its page), placed at the equal-tempered station and then moved once toward the named note, never toward the recording, on E2, E3 and F5; Eb4's finger is not moved

Eb4 rendered at 47944 Hz and resampled to 48 kHz for the page. The rate was chosen on 11-04 against the 48 kHz page of that day (313.41 Hz), to put the period 0.025 samples short of 153, the middle of the range in which a one-string test on this note's string locked to a whole period (153 samples at 47944 Hz is 313.36 Hz, 12.4 c sharp of equal temperament). On the posted clip, with the endpin, the printed bar, 24-layer ribs and the bow force recomputed on that body, the note sounds 313.48 Hz (1.0-2.4 s on the render): a period of 152.94 samples at the render rate, 0.06 short of a whole number, and over the middle half of the clip it ranges over 4.1 c in windows of eight periods

Eb4 plays with the body's wood loss raised 3.25 times; on free decay that takes the shell's lower strong pole from Q 67-75 with wood alone to Q 24-27, read on F5 and C2 renders with the same packs, near the 18-26 printed for a cello on a rig (Zhang and Woodhouse 2014); every other cello page keeps the wood-only loss

on A3, D3, C2, G2, E2, E3, Eb4 and F5, the endpin as a point mass of 186.6 g on the shell: 0.47 m by 8 mm (Sakai and Samejima 2023, Table 3) at the 7900 kg/m3 printed there for iron, solid assumed, shared over the lower end block's 85 by 30 mm footprint from Johannsson's table, a maker's table not measured on this cello; the block's own wood is not added

on A3, D3, C2, G2, E2, E3, Eb4 and F5, the bass bar at its printed place: its ends sit 83.5 and 83.4 mm from the top's ends, against 80 to 85 mm on Alan Goldblatt's cello specification sheet and 80 in a maker's forum post (Cliff Green), after sliding it 12.27 mm toward the neck from where the il Cannone mapping had put it (71.2 and 95.7 mm); its length, height, width, slant and place under the bridge's bass foot are unchanged. Goldblatt's and Johannsson's are makers' tables, borrowed and named, not measurements of this cello

on G2, D3, A3, C2, E2, E3 and F5, the cello's other three strings on the same bridge, unbowed and undamped, so they ring only as the body drives them: on G2 the D3, C2 and A3 strings of Mansour, Woodhouse and Scavone 2016 (D'Addario Kaplan Solutions KS510), each as its own open page plays it but single plane and with 36, 64 and 24 retained bending modes (to 4.1-4.6 kHz; the residual-flexibility row condenses what is left out); on D3 the C2 (64 modes), G2 (56) and A3 (24) strings, single plane (to 4.1-5.0 kHz), C2 and A3 of the same set and G2 the Thomastik-Infeld Dominant that its own open page plays (Lampis, Mayer and Chatziioannou 2024); on A3 the D3 (36 modes), C2 (64) and G2 (52) strings, single plane (to 4.1-4.6 kHz), D3 and C2 of the same set and G2 the Dominant; on C2 the D3 (36 modes), G2 (52) and A3 (24) strings, single plane (to 4.6 kHz), D3 and A3 of the same set and G2 the Dominant; on E2 and E3, their C string stopped by the finger, the same three strings as on C2; on F5, its A string stopped by the finger, the D3, C2 and G2 strings as on A3, with no residual-flexibility row on the card; the bridge joint is the card's 200000 N/m, 0.1 N s/m on each, and the body profile carries four bridge lines (G, D, C, A on G2; D, C, G, A on D3; A, D, C, G on A3 and F5; C, D, G, A on C2, E2 and E3) on the same 24-layer shell table and endpin

a 96 kHz render clock on A3 and F5 (the card's `audio` row reads 96000; the clip is decimated 2:1 to the page's 48 kHz with a zero-phase 801-tap Kaiser FIR, pass band to about 21 kHz, and holds -79.9 dB re total above 24 kHz): the engine's stiffness guard is a fraction of the sample rate, 0.9 pi f_s by the source line, 2.71e5 rad/s at 96 kHz; A3's four-string card, whose bound is 1.145e5 rad/s, was refused at 48 kHz, so the 48 kHz limit is lower than the source line reads (where the factor comes from is not found), and it is admitted at 96 kHz. On A3's one-string card on 24-layer ribs the clock moves the harmonics while the note builds, by up to 12.8 dB over 0.5-1.2 s (within 0.8 dB over 1.0-1.9 s), takes its body line 10.7 dB lower and costs the count one row (brightness crosses its ruler outward); on F5, whose card has no residual-flexibility row, the three-string card's bound is 1.4392e5 rad/s (the one-string card's 1.2230e5), above the 48 kHz line, and it was not run at 48 kHz; on F5's one-string card the clock leaves the count at 6 of 15, takes harmonics-to-noise from 44.4 to 48.0 dB (recording 27.6) and puts a held line at 246.6 Hz at -48.0 dB re the first harmonic where the 48 kHz page reads -66.4 dB at 248.1 Hz, moving
physics_missing: a measured cello: the body is computed from published geometry and wood data, and no measured body admittance or string Q of this instrument is on the cards; on the C2 page the wood data are stated only from 150 Hz (maple) and 100 Hz (spruce), so that body has no mode below 150 Hz, above the C2 fundamental

body modes above the computed range: 256 modes end at 2438.5 Hz (2209.9 Hz in the modal run on the 24-layer ribs of C2, E2, E3, G2, Eb4 and F5; the 512 modes of D3 ended at about 4.3 kHz on 6-layer ribs; the 512 modes of D3 and A3 on 24-layer ribs not read); the plates are resolved to about 3 kHz and the 6-layer ribs not above about 1 kHz

body damping: the shell's lowest strong pole reads Q 72-78 from wood alone (free decay 67-75, receiver sweep 78), against 18 to 26 printed for a cello on a rig or foam and 13.4 held by a player (Zhang and Woodhouse 2014); the F5 page names this as a likely reason for its fault, not shown. The wood loss raised 3.25 times toward the printed damping was tried on all eight cello pages: one rose (Eb4, 10 to 11 of 14) and it darkened every page, bringing the three too-bright pages toward their recordings and the five too-dark ones away. So more wood loss isn't what the cello's top end is missing
a body-radiation skin row: the posted cards carry none

a bow that varies during the note: force and speed hold after the ramp (D3's and A3's force follows speed only through the start), so the notes repeat too exactly: harmonics-to-noise reads 37.7 dB against 30.1 in the recording on C2 (39.8 with the other three strings on its bridge) and 43.2 against 30.1 on E2 (31.4 with the other three strings on its bridge) and 29.2 against 24.3 on E3 (26.4 with the other three strings on its bridge) (Eb4, with the printed wood loss, its bow at 1/11, 24-layer ribs and its force recomputed on that body, reads 38.6 against 37.9, where its 6-layer page read 41.8); the Eb4 attack, 437 ms against 411 before its force was recomputed and 342 on its 6-layer page, reads 118 ms with it

time-step independence: at 48 kHz a note's period can lock to the render clock and put lines into the sound that are not in the instrument; Eb4 needed its own render rate, and F5 held a line at exactly a third of its pitch (233.0 Hz, -28.8 dB) until its bow moved to 1/11 of its sounding length, which removed it; A3 renders at 96 kHz, where its period, 434.92 samples, is 0.09 from a whole number and ranges over 2.2 samples across the clip, so it does not sit on one whole-sample period, and no read decides whether the 96 kHz clock leaves lines that are not in the instrument; F5, rendered at 96 kHz for its three strings, shows on its one-string 96 kHz control a held line at 246.6 Hz (-48.0 dB re its first harmonic) that its 48 kHz page does not, and the line is not traced

an explanation of the finger: the bowed pitch moves 1.4 to 1.8 times the length of the move (on 6-layer ribs: E3 25.3 c for 17.6 c before its residual row, which takes a further 4.5 c off the note on the page rendered 11-05, E2 19.2 c for 10.7 c before its row, which takes a further 4.8 c up), so E2 and E3 land flat of equal temperament, and the E3 and F5 recordings sit sharp of it

the bow's omitted-mode compliance on a stopped note: the engine refuses `bow-residual-flexibility` with a finger stop (the bow/stop cross-compliance is not yet carried), so E2 and E3 have the support row only and Eb4 and F5 have neither row; F5 was tried with the support row and fell from 9 to 8 of 15 (harmonics-to-noise left its ruler, the third harmonic rose to 23.7 dB re the first, and a held line appeared at 189 Hz, -19 dB), so it stays without

the timbre balance: the low notes and A3 are too dark (centroid 203 Hz against 388 on C2 with the other three strings on its bridge, 217 without them, 196 against 390 on E2 (199 with the other three strings on its bridge), 230 against 575 on E3 (272 with the other three strings on its bridge), 353 against 868 on A3's 6-layer 48 kHz page, 323 against 868 with the three strings, 24-layer ribs and the 96 kHz clock, where its fourth harmonic is 15.1 dB under the recording's and above 5 kHz it reads -59.7 dB re total against -26.8) and F5 too bright on its 6-layer page (1587 against 1187; 1267 with the endpin, the printed bar and 24-layer ribs, 1245 with its force recomputed on that body and 1233 with the other three strings on its bridge at 96 kHz; Eb4, with the printed wood loss, its bow at 1/11, 24-layer ribs and its force recomputed on that body, is 468 against 466 (499 before the force was recomputed; its 6-layer page 466)); D3's first two harmonics are swapped without the other strings on its bridge (H2 4.6 dB over H1, the recording 7.5 dB under, on 6-layer ribs) and in the recording's order with them (10.3 dB under on 6-layer ribs, 9.1 dB under on 24-layer ribs, 1.0-2.4 s), where its centroid is 311 Hz on 6-layer ribs and 403 Hz on 24-layer ribs against 215, and its third harmonic sits 12.2 and 16.6 dB over the recording's; on the 6-layer F5 page the second and third harmonics sit 3.8 and 3.6 dB over the first (the third 15.7 dB over it before), and with the endpin, the printed bar, 24-layer ribs and its force recomputed on that body 5.1 dB over and 10.3 dB under it, the recording 4.6 and 5.9 dB under it (0.7-1.7 s)

the stopped notes' bow: E3 at 1/11 and the page's 0.4204 N broke to its octave (0.90 times Schelleng's minimum, rendered 11-04). With the bow at 1/11 the E3 holes at H4 and H5 did not close (they moved -0.8 and +2.7 dB re the first on the 6-layer page rendered 11-05), and they sit in a valley of that 6-layer shell's bridge mobility at 818-870 Hz; on the posted E3 clip, with the endpin, the printed bar, 24-layer ribs and its force recomputed on that body, H4 and H5 sit 14.0 and 25.3 dB under the recording's re the first (0.7-1.4 s; 11.7 and 24.9 dB with the other three strings on its bridge); E2, with the endpin, the printed bar and 24-layer ribs and its stopped string alone, holds its level within 0.5 dB from 0.2 to 2.4 s, its second harmonic leads its first by 8.4 dB (+5.5 in the recording, 0.5-1.4 s), and its burst near the body's 190 Hz mode, which no grader row measures, reads -59.7 dB re the strongest bin over 1.0-1.7 s (the recording shows nothing there above -51.7 dB); with the other three strings on its bridge E2 holds its level within 1.5 dB, not 0.5, its second harmonic is 1.4 dB under its first, and the burst reads -42.4 dB at 187.4 Hz; F5 at 1/11 with 0.33 N, on the 6-layer page rendered 11-06, is clean in its motion (no octave, no subharmonic) but reads 34.6 dB harmonics-to-noise against 27.6 in the recording, and its harmonics-to-noise, cepstral and harmonics rows left their rulers while wavelet, odd/even and attack came in (9 of 15 both ways); with the endpin, the printed bar and 24-layer ribs and the same force it reads 41.1 dB, and its waveform resembles itself at half its period (autocorrelation +0.54 there over 0.7-1.7 s, the 6-layer page -0.15, the recording -0.54), with no subharmonic, and with its force recomputed on that body (0.417 N) it reads 44.4 dB and +0.49 at half its period; Eb4 at 1/11 with 0.29 N, on the 6-layer page rendered 11-06, is clean in its motion (no octave, no subharmonic, one full slip per period as before, with more small slips between them: 8.2, 2.8 and 12.0 slip events per period on its three bow cells against 2.1, 2.0 and 4.0) and ties its page at 11 of 14 (attack comes inside, cepstral envelope goes outside), but it now reads 41.8 dB harmonics-to-noise against 37.9 in the recording and holds a line at 301.3 Hz, -39.1 dB re its first harmonic, where the last page read -57.5 dB. The stopped notes' force is a rule chosen for these pages, the window's geometric mean (on E3, Eb4 and F5 computed by the engine on each page's own shell in vacuo, on E2 from the earlier body's shell table, since the engine refuses E2's f0); the open pages' forces sit higher (0.78 to 0.80 on a log scale); a measured player's bow force for a stopped cello note at a known bow distance would replace the rule

lines that are not harmonics: C2's line near 175 Hz, on its bowed string alone, reads 176.8 Hz, 23.4 dB over the recording over 0.5-1.4 s, and its line near 163.9 Hz reads 165.4 Hz, 8.8 dB over the recording's there; with the other three strings the 175 Hz line reads 177.2 Hz at -38.6 dB re the strongest bin, 4.5 dB lower than the -34.1 dB the same read gives without them (both move with a shifted window), and the 164 Hz line was not re-read; neither is traced; Eb4's line at 301.3 Hz, 12.2 Hz under its note, read -46.4 dB re its first harmonic over 0.72-2.17 s with the endpin, the printed bar and 24-layer ribs (-39.1 dB on the 6-layer page), and with its force recomputed on that body it reads -52.0 dB at 301.1 Hz, while a line as far over the note, 325.7 Hz, rises from -49.7 to -47.3 dB and is now its strongest that is not a harmonic; the recording's strongest bins there are 301.8 Hz at -57.9 dB and 326.1 Hz at -56.9 dB; the 6-layer page matched the 301 Hz line in frequency to a shell mode near 300 Hz, but in the modal run that mode moves from 300.5 to 294.9 Hz from 6 to 24 layers (the bar moved on both) and the line does not, so neither line is traced; summed over 165-195 Hz its cluster reads -27.7 dB re its first harmonic (-30.6 dB before the force was recomputed, -32.3 dB on the 6-layer page), against -32.7 dB in the recording; no grader row measures either

the other strings: only G2 (D3, C2 and A3 on its bridge), D3 (C2, G2 and A3 on its bridge), A3 (D3, C2 and G2 on its bridge) C2 (D3, G2 and A3 on its bridge) and E2 and E3 (the same three, each with its C string stopped by the finger) and F5 (D3, C2 and G2, its A string stopped by the finger, at a 96 kHz clock) carry them, unbowed and undamped; every other page has only its bowed string, so there is no sympathetic ringing or string-to-string coupling through the body there, and the strings added have no torsion, no fingers and no dampers.
